facts: Southern hairy-nosed wombats live in groups, sharing warrens: networks of burrows with many entrances.
They live in the dry scrub and grasslands of southern South Australia and the Nullarbor Plain.
They shelter underground through the heat of the day and come out to graze at night.
They mostly eat native grasses, and get almost all the water they need from their food.
Their name comes from the fine hairs on their nose. Common wombats have bare noses.
A wombat's pouch faces backwards, so no soil gets in while it digs.
Invasive plants crowd out the native grasses that wombats rely on.
